intro: Hi! In this lesson you'll learn words for jobs and workplaces, hobbies and sports, and things people do at the weekend, so you can say 'I'm a teacher. I work in a school. On Sundays I go cycling.' Warm-up: what do you do, and what do you do in your free time?
teachingNotes: Teach the words in small themed groups with an Indonesian gloss (jobs, workplaces, play / go activities, other hobbies, weekend activities) and practise them in short simple present sentences with real Indonesian contexts (kantor, sekolah, warung, Bandung, Jakarta).

A job needs a/an: 'I am a teacher', 'She's an engineer' (common error: *'I am teacher', because Indonesian says 'Saya guru'). 'What do you do?' asks about your job (Apa pekerjaanmu?). A cook is a person; a cooker is a stove (kompor), so never *'He is a cooker'.

Workplaces: work in a hospital / an office / a shop / a school / a bank / a restaurant / a factory, but work on a farm. Accept 'at' (at a bank, at a school) too. 'Ibu rumah tangga' is a homemaker / stay-at-home mum if a learner asks.

play + ball sports, games and instruments (play football, play badminton, play chess, play the guitar); go + -ing activities (go swimming, go cycling, go fishing, go shopping). Indonesian 'main' and 'pergi' cause the errors *'I play swimming' and *'I go to shopping': correct them. Mention 'do' (do yoga, do karate) only if the learner asks.

After 'My hobby is' use -ing or a noun: 'My hobby is playing football', 'My hobby is music' (common error: *'My hobby is play football'). 'In my free time I + verb' uses the simple present. Learners have not studied like + -ing yet: accept 'I like swimming' if they use it, but don't drill it here.

Weekend: at the weekend (British) and on the weekend (American) are both correct; on Saturday / on Sundays; go to + a place (go to the mall, go to the beach) but go + -ing for activities. Say watch TV, not *'see TV'. Limits: simple present only (he/she + -s), no past simple, no future forms.

keyPoints.title: Jobs and workplaces
keyPoints.explanation: Say your job with a/an: I'm a nurse, She's an engineer. Ask with What do you do? Say where with work in: work in a hospital, an office, a shop, a school, a bank, a factory. A farm is different: work on a farm.

examples.en: What do you do? — I'm a teacher.
My mother is a nurse. She works in a hospital.
examples.id: Ibu saya perawat. Dia bekerja di rumah sakit.

examples.en: Pak Made is a farmer. He works on a farm in Bali.
examples.id: Pak Made petani. Dia bekerja di ladang di Bali.

keyPoints.title: Hobbies and sports: play or go?
keyPoints.explanation: Use play with ball sports, games and instruments: play football, play chess, play the guitar. Use go with -ing activities: go swimming, go cycling, go fishing, go shopping. After My hobby is use -ing: My hobby is reading.

examples.id: Kami main bulu tangkis setiap hari Jumat.

examples.en: My cousin goes swimming on Saturdays.
examples.id: Sepupu saya berenang setiap hari Sabtu.

keyPoints.title: Weekend activities
keyPoints.explanation: Talk about your weekend with the simple present: At the weekend I visit my grandparents. On Sundays we clean the house. Use go to + a place (go to the beach) but go + -ing for an activity (go shopping).

examples.en: At the weekend I visit my grandparents.
examples.id: Di akhir pekan saya mengunjungi kakek nenek.

examples.en: On Saturdays Budi goes to the market with his mother.
examples.id: Setiap hari Sabtu Budi pergi ke pasar dengan ibunya.

examples.en: On Sunday mornings we stay at home.
examples.id: Setiap Minggu pagi kami di rumah saja.

blocks.text: To ask about someone's job, say **What do you do?** It's a fixed question: it means 'What's your job?', not 'What are you doing now?'. Answer with **I'm a / I'm an** + job: *I'm a nurse.* (*I'm* = I am.) Use **an** when the job starts with a **vowel sound**, that is, when you say it, it starts with a, e, i, o or u: **an engineer**, **an office worker**. Then say where you work: **I work in a hospital.**

id.text: Untuk menanyakan pekerjaan seseorang, ucapkan **What do you do?** Ini pertanyaan tetap: artinya 'Apa pekerjaanmu?', bukan 'Kamu sedang apa?'. Jawab dengan **I'm a / I'm an** + pekerjaan: *I'm a nurse.* (*I'm* = I am.) Pakai **an** kalau pekerjaannya diawali **bunyi vokal**, yaitu waktu diucapkan, bunyi awalnya a, e, i, o atau u: **an engineer**, **an office worker**. Lalu sebutkan tempat kerjamu: **I work in a hospital.**

rows.note: work ON a farm (just remember it)

blocks.text: Indonesian says *Saya guru*, with no 'adalah' and no 'seorang'. English needs both: **am** (in *I'm*) and **a/an** before one job: **I'm a teacher**, never 'I'm teacher' or 'I teacher'. For more than one person, use the plural with no a/an: *They're teachers.* And a **cook** is a person (juru masak); a **cooker** is a stove (kompor)!

id.text: Bahasa Indonesia bilang *Saya guru*, tanpa 'adalah' dan tanpa 'seorang'. Bahasa Inggris butuh dua-duanya: **am** (di dalam *I'm*) dan **a/an** sebelum satu pekerjaan: **I'm a teacher**, bukan 'I'm teacher' atau 'I teacher'. Untuk lebih dari satu orang, pakai bentuk jamak tanpa a/an: *They're teachers.* Dan **cook** itu orang (juru masak); **cooker** itu kompor!

blocks.explain: A job needs a/an after I'm: I'm a teacher. 'I teacher' has no am (I'm = I am), and English always needs it.

id.explain: Pekerjaan butuh a/an setelah I'm: I'm a teacher. 'I teacher' tidak punya am (I'm = I am), padahal bahasa Inggris selalu membutuhkannya.

blocks.text:
Indonesian says *main* for many things, but English has two verbs (doing words). Use **play** with ball sports, games and instruments: **play football**, **play badminton**, **play chess**, **play the guitar**. Use **go** with activities that end in **-ing**: **go swimming**, **go cycling**, **go fishing**, **go shopping**.

One small surprise: instruments take **the** (*play **the** guitar, play **the** piano*), but sports and games don't (*play football, play chess*). There's no logic to learn here: just remember it.

id.text:
Bahasa Indonesia bilang *main* untuk banyak hal, tapi bahasa Inggris punya dua kata kerja. Pakai **play** untuk olahraga dengan bola, permainan dan alat musik: **play football**, **play badminton**, **play chess**, **play the guitar**. Pakai **go** untuk kegiatan yang berakhiran **-ing**: **go swimming**, **go cycling**, **go fishing**, **go shopping**.

Satu hal kecil yang mengejutkan: alat musik pakai **the** (*play **the** guitar, play **the** piano*), tapi olahraga dan permainan tidak (*play football, play chess*). Tidak ada logika khusus: hafalkan saja.

rows.id: Kami main bulu tangkis setiap hari Jumat.

rows.en: My cousin goes swimming on Saturdays.
rows.id: Sepupu saya berenang setiap hari Sabtu.

rows.en: I go cycling with my neighbours.

blocks.text:
Never say 'play swimming' or 'go to shopping'. With **-ing** activities use **go** and no **to**: **I go swimming**, **we go shopping**. *To* is only for a place (*go **to** the beach*), and swimming or shopping is an activity, not a place.

Remember the **-s** with he/she (one person): **He plays**. Some words add **-es** instead: **go → goes**, **watch → watches** (*Budi watches films*). It's the same -s idea; the e just makes it easier to say.

id.text:
Jangan bilang 'play swimming' atau 'go to shopping'. Untuk kegiatan **-ing** pakai **go** tanpa **to**: **I go swimming**, **we go shopping**. *To* hanya untuk tempat (*go **to** the beach*), sedangkan swimming atau shopping itu kegiatan, bukan tempat.

Ingat **-s** untuk he/she (satu orang): **He plays**. Beberapa kata ditambah **-es**: **go → goes**, **watch → watches** (*Budi watches films*). Idenya sama dengan -s; huruf e hanya supaya lebih mudah diucapkan.

blocks.explain: Swimming ends in -ing, so use go, with no 'to': I go swimming.

id.explain: Swimming berakhiran -ing, jadi pakai go, tanpa 'to': I go swimming.

blocks.text: Say what you usually do in your free time with the normal present form (the **simple present**: *I read, she reads*): **In my free time I read.** Or say **My hobby is** + a verb with **-ing**: **My hobby is reading.** **My hobby is playing football.**

id.text: Ceritakan apa yang biasa kamu lakukan di waktu luang dengan bentuk biasa (**simple present**: *I read, she reads*): **In my free time I read.** Atau ucapkan **My hobby is** + kata kerja dengan **-ing**: **My hobby is reading.** **My hobby is playing football.**

rows.en: In my free time I listen to music.
rows.id: Di waktu luang saya mendengarkan musik.

rows.en: Budi watches films in his free time.
rows.id: Budi menonton film di waktu luangnya.

blocks.text: Indonesian *Hobi saya main bola* has no -ing, but English needs it: **My hobby is playing football**, not 'My hobby is play football'. Why? After **is** you need the **name** of an activity, and adding **-ing** turns a doing word into that name: *play* (main) → *playing* (kegiatan bermain), *read* → *reading*, *cook* → *cooking*.

id.text: *Hobi saya main bola* tidak memakai -ing, tapi bahasa Inggris membutuhkannya: **My hobby is playing football**, bukan 'My hobby is play football'. Kenapa? Setelah **is** kamu perlu **nama** kegiatannya, dan tambahan **-ing** mengubah kata kerja jadi nama kegiatan: *play* (main) → *playing* (kegiatan bermain), *read* → *reading*, *cook* → *cooking*.

blocks.explain: After My hobby is, use the -ing form: My hobby is cooking.

id.explain: Setelah My hobby is, pakai bentuk -ing: My hobby is cooking.

blocks.text: Saturday and Sunday are **the weekend**. Say **at the weekend** (British) or **on the weekend** (American): both are correct. Say **on Saturday** for one Saturday, and **on Sundays** (with -s) for every Sunday. Use the simple present for things you often do: **At the weekend I visit my grandparents.**

id.text: Sabtu dan Minggu adalah **the weekend** (akhir pekan). Ucapkan **at the weekend** (Inggris) atau **on the weekend** (Amerika): dua-duanya benar. Ucapkan **on Saturday** untuk satu hari Sabtu, dan **on Sundays** (pakai -s) untuk setiap hari Minggu. Pakai simple present (bentuk biasa) untuk kegiatan yang sering kamu lakukan: **At the weekend I visit my grandparents.**

rows.en: go to the beach / go to the mall
rows.id: pergi ke pantai / pergi ke mal

blocks.text:
**go to** + a place: **go to the mall**, **go to the market**. **go** + -ing for an activity: **go shopping**. And you **watch** TV, you don't 'see' TV.

British and American words you may hear: **film** (UK) = **movie** (US); **football** (UK) = **soccer** (US); **neighbour** (UK spelling) = **neighbor** (US spelling). Both are fine.

id.text:
**go to** + tempat: **go to the mall**, **go to the market**. **go** + -ing untuk kegiatan: **go shopping**. Dan kita **watch** TV, bukan 'see' TV.

Kata Inggris (UK) dan Amerika (US) yang mungkin kamu dengar: **film** (UK) = **movie** (US); **football** (UK) = **soccer** (US); **neighbour** (ejaan UK) = **neighbor** (ejaan US). Dua-duanya benar.

blocks.prompt: Complete: On Saturday I ___ to the beach with my family.
blocks.explain: go to + a place: go to the beach. You visit a person or a place without 'to'.

id.explain: go to + tempat: go to the beach. Visit dipakai tanpa 'to' (visit my grandparents).
